newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Boosey shares hum on bid talk.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Boosey shares hum on bid talk.

text.p: Shares in British musical instrument-maker and publisher Boosey & Hawkes Plc hit a year high on Thursday following news that major shareholder Carl Fischer Inc had put its 45.3 percent stake up for sale.
They hit a high of 905 pence before easing back to 895 in the afternoon, up 27-1/2 pence on the day. That followed a 70 pence gain on Wednesday when Boosey announced Carl Fischer's intentions.

Richard Holland, Boosey chief executive, told Reuters he wanted to keep the group's independence. "My own preference is for the company to remain independent. It's done rather well under that status," he said. But he told Reuters: "Carl Fischer is in the driving seat." There had been no tentative approaches since Wednesday's announcement, he added.
Any group acquiring the stake held by Fischer, a privately-owned U.S. music publisher, would have to make a full bid for the company under British takeover rules.
Boosey, one of the best-known players in the classical music market, has said it is discussing alternative proposals with advisers Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
But the possibility of a bid has excited the market, although no list of potential predators sprang forward from analysts.
Boosey's interests span making woodwind and brass instruments to classical music publishing. Its catalogue of music includes compositions by composers including Rachmaninov and Stravinsky.

The group said on Wednesday that any alternative plans it put forward would aim to "provide shareholders of Carl Fischer with liquidity and shareholders of Boosey & Hawkes with a continuing interest in a listed company".
Holland refused to elaborate on whether it was considering a takeover of Fischer, or a possible merger.
But Boosey has admitted in the past it has ambitions for acquisition-led growth and has delivered a quick rate of expansion for shareholders in the last eight years.

In that period its market capitalisation has rocketed to 156 million pounds from nine million. It has also delivered compound earnings per share and dividend growth of 20 percent over the eight years.
The 1996 results showed profits up 25 percent to 7.7 million pounds ($12.5 million), making Holland confident that if it wanted to fund a deal it had the financial credentials to go to the market.
"We can fund small deals out of existing borrowings. A larger deal would mean raising more equity but our standing in the market is so high that it would be easy to do," he said.
He denied that a legal action brought by Boosey against leisure giant Walt Disney Co would affect its future plans, because all legal costs were written off continually.

Boosey alleges Disney infringed its copyright on Stravinsky's "The Rite of Spring", used in the U.S. group's "Fantasia". Holland has said he is confident of being backed again in the appeal courts but has declined to name the sum of money at stake. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
